task: Price agent.subagent.usage totals into cost_daily for agents without request rows, log/count CLI analytics ingest project-gate discards with reason, and relax the cost_daily inner join in get_session_cost_facts, with live-DB tests.

key_reasoning.reason: Three independent changes: rollups (totals pricing into cost_daily, model-price lookup), ingestor/project gate (discard logging and counting), reader (get_session_cost_facts join). Plus storage guide update.

Goals are named, but the pricing design is open: price source, how to avoid double counting with request rows, behaviour for cost_daily columns, backfill of existing totals, counter mechanism and what a session with no cost rows should show. Scope option (b) was called invasive by backend research.

Closest pattern is the _LOG-family cost_daily build from _cli_requests, which has no precedent for token-priced totals. Mistakes double count cost on KPI dashboards, and rollups are SQL strings mostly asserted by string tests, so live-DB tests are needed. Relaxing the reader inner join changes the session list and developer/cost aggregation semantics. _totals_are_a_source must stay strict. No security-sensitive input handling; the gate-discard logging must avoid leaking project/user data.
Estimated 8-10 modified (rollups.py, reader.py, ingestor.py, possibly gate/router, storage guide, existing tests) and 2-3 new live-DB test files, across 3+ directories.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped to XL: pricing/cost semantics change in shared rollups with double-count risk and no exact precedent
Requires data semantics change in cost_daily: affects existing rollup recompute/backfill
